input: Plan a guided museum tour for the kids

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The type of museum (science, art, history, natural history, etc.) completely changes the content, exhibits to prioritise, and how the tour is structured.
The number of children and their ages determines pacing, language complexity, group management, and whether special supervision ratios are needed.
Whether this is a school trip, birthday outing, family visit, or community event affects formality, permissions, scheduling, and logistics.
The available budget determines whether to hire a professional guide, use self-guided materials, or rely on free museum educator programmes.
The target date and duration shape how much preparation time is available and how long the tour itself should run to keep kids engaged.
Knowing whether the tour should be interactive (hands-on activities, Q&A games) vs. more traditional narration changes the format and materials needed.
Understanding the primary goal — educational learning outcomes, fun and engagement, or a mix — defines what a successful tour looks like and how to measure it.

gold.taskTitle: Plan a guided museum tour for kids
gold.taskDescription: Organise a guided museum tour experience designed specifically for children.

questions.title: What type of museum are you planning to visit?
questions.description: Identify the museum category — science, natural history, art, history, or a specific institution — to shape the tour content and exhibit selection.

questions.title: How many kids are attending, and what are their ages?
questions.description: Determine group size and age range to calibrate pacing, language, supervision needs, and engagement techniques.

questions.title: What is the occasion — school trip, family outing, or other?
questions.description: Clarify the setting and context of the visit to align formality, permissions, and overall structure of the tour.

questions.title: What is your budget for the tour experience?
questions.description: Establish financial limits to decide between hiring a professional guide, using museum-provided educators, or building a self-guided plan.

questions.title: When is the tour happening and how long should it run?
questions.description: Pin down the target date and intended duration to manage preparation time and keep the tour within kids' attention spans.

questions.title: Should the tour be hands-on and interactive or more traditional?
questions.description: Determine the preferred style — activity-based, storytelling, Q&A games, or classic narrated walkthrough — to design the right format.

questions.title: Is the main goal learning outcomes, pure fun, or both equally?
questions.description: Identify the primary success measure so the tour can be evaluated and designed around what matters most to the organiser.
